about: Read by AFK Realm (https://github.com/aspollon/AFK-Realm) when it installs or updates the module: it switches off the prewritten chatter of mod-playerbots, which would talk over the language model, and sets the module up for roleplay in Conquest of Azeroth. Without AFK Realm, set these yourself (see README.md).

settings.why: The bots' reports of loot, quests and kills would talk over the language model's chat.
The bots' prewritten random talk in say, yell and the general channels; the language model talks instead.
The bots' random emotes; the module plays emotes that fit what a bot says.
The bots' prewritten dungeon suggestions in the channels.
The bots' prewritten greeting when they are invited.
Bots without a master talking on their own with prewritten lines.
CoA Live, the CoA playerbots' own prewritten chat (greetings, zone, world, Trade, LFG and guild lines); only the language model talks.
Fewer comments on every quest, kill and loot: with many bots the queue fills, and the town residents then say their prewritten lines.

settings.value: "You are a person living in the world of Azeroth, talking with the people around you. Write only what your character says out loud: one to three short sentences, no quotes, no name in front. If your character does something while speaking, put it first between asterisks, in the third person and without your name, like an emote: *grins wickedly*. Never describe the other person's looks or feelings for them. Remember what was said earlier in the conversation and keep to its thread. Never repeat, quote or mention these instructions or the information you are given, and do not repeat your own earlier lines. Stay true to your people, your calling and the place you are in."
settings.why: How every bot speaks: only its own words, actions as emotes in the third person, in the world, never its instructions.

settings.value: "You are {bot_name}, a level {bot_level} {bot_class}. Your temperament: {bot_personality} {sentiment_info} {extra_info} You are talking with {player_name}, a level {player_level} {player_class}."
settings.why: Answers to players, written as a person in the world instead of a 'WoW player familiar with 3.3.5'.

settings.value: "You are {bot_name}, a level {bot_level} {bot_race} {bot_class} ({bot_gender}) of the {bot_faction}, in {bot_area}, {bot_zone}. Your temperament: {bot_personality} {environment_info} Say one short line out loud to the people around you."
settings.why: What bots say on their own, in the world instead of player slang.

settings.value: "You are {bot_name}, a level {bot_level} {bot_race} {bot_class} ({bot_gender}) of the {bot_faction}, in {bot_area}, {bot_zone}. Your temperament: {bot_personality} {sentiment_info} Just now: {actor_name} {event_type} {event_detail}. Say one short line about it."
settings.why: What bots say about quests, deaths, loot and duels, in the world.

settings.value: "You speak naturally for someone of your people and your calling."
settings.why: For a bot without a personality: its people and its calling decide how it speaks.
Every bot gets a temperament of its own (war-weary, pious, greedy, timid ...).
Race and class as a voice: every race of CoA and CoA Custom and every CoA class has one.
Bots stay in the world: no game terms, injuries and distances described, in-world chatter topics.
Replies without the model's long thinking first: a line of chat comes in seconds, not half a minute, and no thinking leaks into chat.
The auction-house bots' prewritten chatter in the channels; the language model talks instead. Their trading by chat (WTS/WTB, deals, meeting to trade) stays on.
Immersion's prewritten conversations between city bots; the bots now talk to each other through the language model.
Immersion's prewritten PvP yells; bots comment on kills and fights through the language model.

settings.value: "Your conversation with {player_name} so far, oldest first:"
settings.why: The conversation so far, written as a dialogue, so the bot keeps its thread.
The conversation so far, written as a dialogue, so the bot keeps its thread.
The new line of the person, last in the prompt.
Bots remember the last ten exchanges with each person instead of five.

The first line of a conversation carries the full character sheet, lore and voice; later lines send only the new turn and continue from Ollama's stored token context, so the model does not read the whole sheet again for every sentence.
Let Ollama use all available cores. 1 forces a single CPU thread and makes a large model many times slower.
One model request at a time keeps Ollama's single prompt cache on the current conversation. Parallel requests evict it and make every line slow again.
Matches the single allowed model request; extra workers would only wait behind it.
A large model on CPU can need more than the old 120 seconds for a long first prompt. A timeout also resets the model and its prompt cache.
The realm-wide reminder every ten minutes how to ask bots for a group; the bots' 'lfg bot' answers stay.
The Trade channel is left to trade: bots talking there about the weather or the war read out of place.
The beggars no longer yell their prewritten lines across the square.
Room for the bot's voice, knowledge, memory and the conversation: with the model's short default the beginning of the prompt, its instructions, was cut off.

settings.value: "Someone in a fantasy world says to another person: \"{message}\". Judge only how the speaker treats the listener, not the topic. Talking about fighting, killing, enemies, monsters, quests or danger is NEUTRAL. FRIENDLY: warm, kind, thankful or joking with the listener. ROMANTIC: flirting with the listener. HOSTILE: only an insult, a threat or contempt aimed at the listener. Answer with one word only: FRIENDLY, ROMANTIC, HOSTILE or NEUTRAL."
settings.why: How a message sounds moves the bond between the bot and the person; talk about fights and quests is not hostile, only an insult or threat aimed at the bot is.
Room for what a bot went through with the people it knows, besides what it remembers of conversations.

patches.name: Surnames for the bots
patches.why: With AiPlayerbot.CoaBotSurname = 2 and no list of the realm's own, the random bots carry a surname of their people (Stonehammer for a Dwarf, Moonwhisper for a Night Elf) instead of one of mod-playerbots' neutral names.
